rubrik: Developing the tax on chemicals in certain electronics
dok_titel: GDP indexation of taxes on chemicals in certain electronics and waste incineration
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both MP).
notis:
The Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to adjust two taxes in relation to the development of gross domestic product (GDP), a so-called GDP indexation. The government's proposal concerns the tax on chemicals in certain electronics and the tax on waste incineration. The change proposed by the government would mean that the taxes are adjusted taking into account both changes in the consumer price index (CPI) and the development of gross domestic product (GDP).
The Riksdag considers that the evaluations carried out of the taxes have shown that they have not been sufficiently effective in achieving the goals that were their purpose. The Riksdag also notes that the government has proposed that the tax on waste incineration be abolished in January 2023. Against this background, the Riksdag said no to the government's proposal to recalculate these taxes based on the GDP index.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:11 by Linus Lakso and Emma Nohrén (both MP).
Dissenting opinion 3

dok_titel: Freedom of association and terrorist organizations (dormant constitutional amendment proposal)
forslag_text: The Riksdag finally adopts the dormant proposal in Appendix 2 for an act amending the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen).
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to a constitutional amendment proposal that entails expanded possibilities to restrict, through ordinary legislation, the freedom of association of organizations that engage in or support terrorism.
The proposal is a so-called dormant constitutional amendment proposal (vilande grundlagsförslag), which means that the Riksdag has already made a decision on the matter on a previous occasion. To amend a constitutional law, the Riksdag is required to vote identically twice on the proposal and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the proposal was made on 6 April 2022, when the Riksdag voted yes.
The legislative amendment is to enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives: The Riksdag finally adopts the dormant proposal in Appendix 2 for an act amending the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen).
Dissenting opinion 1

rubrik: Amendments to the Code of Judicial Procedure
dok_titel: Foreign espionage (dormant constitutional amendment proposal etc.)
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for an act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure (rättegångsbalken) in the parts concerning Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the legislative proposal in other respects with the amendment that
a) 27 Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording proposed by the committee in Appendix 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially approves Government Bill 2021/22:55 point 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's proposals for legislative amendments and constitutional amendments. The constitutional amendments are a so-called dormant proposal, which means that the Riksdag had already made a decision on that part on a previous occasion.
The legislative proposals mean, among other things, that foreign espionage (utlandsspioneri), aggravated foreign espionage, and aggravated unauthorized handling of secret information based on foreign espionage are criminalized and incorporated into the Penal Code (brottsbalken).
The Riksdag also said yes to the dormant proposal on amendments to the two constitutional laws the Freedom of the Press Act (tryckfrihetsförordningen) and the Fundamental Law on Freedom of Expression (yttrandefrihetsgrundlagen). The amendments mean, among other things, that foreign espionage and those forms of unauthorized handling of secret information and negligent handling of secret information that are based on foreign espionage are also criminalized as press and freedom of expression offences.
The legislative amendments also entail restrictions on the freedom to communicate information and the freedom to procure information (meddelarfriheten and anskaffarfriheten), i.e. the right to communicate and procure information for publication in media forms protected by constitutional law.
Since the proposal in certain parts concerns amendments to constitutional laws, the Riksdag is required to vote identically twice and there must be an election between the votes. The first decision on the constitutional amendment proposal was made on 6 April 2022, when the Riksdag voted yes. Since then there has been a general election.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the government's proposal for an act amending the Code of Judicial Procedure (rättegångsbalken) in the parts concerning Chapter 27, Section 2, and adopts the legislative proposal in other respects with the amendment that
a) Chapter 27, Sections 18, 20 d and 33 shall have the wording proposed by the committee in Appendix 4, 
b) the preamble shall have the wording that follows from this. 
Thereby the Riksdag partially approves Government Bill 2021/22:55 point 4.
Dissenting opinion 2

rubrik: Guidelines for the Seventh AP Fund
dok_titel: The default option within the premium pension
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:22 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V).
notis:
The government has proposed legislative amendments concerning the Seventh AP Fund (Sjunde AP-fonden) and the management of premium pension assets for those who have not themselves chosen pension funds — the so-called default option (förvalsalternativet). The Riksdag approved the amendments.
The amendments include, among other things, that

the objective of the default option within the premium pension is pension saving of high quality that provides a secure pension, that is, the same objective as for the premium pension system as a whole
a sustainability objective is introduced for the Seventh AP Fund, meaning that fund management shall be conducted in an exemplary manner
there shall be greater scope to invest the fund's assets in so-called illiquid assets.

In the proposal the government also addresses matters concerning the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority's (Finansinspektionen's) supervision of the Seventh AP Fund and freedom of communication (meddelarfrihet) for information within the AP funds' investment operations.
The legislative amendments are to enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:22 by Ida Gabrielsson et al. (V).

2021/22:4768 by Ali Esbati et al. (V) items 1–8 and 

2021/22:4769 by Elisabeth Svantesson et al. (M) items 1–4 and 

files government communication 2021/22:247.
notis:
In a government communication (skrivelse) the previous government reports on the work of implementing Agenda 2030 and the global goals for sustainable development adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2015.
The communication follows from the Riksdag having, in a formal request (tillkännagivande), called on the government to submit every other year a report on the implementation and target attainment of the work on Agenda 2030. The communication now submitted is the first in the series.
In the communication the previous government assesses that 35 of the 169 sub-targets for achieving Agenda 2030 have been fully attained, or have been attained within Sweden.
For 60 of the sub-targets the previous government assesses that further measures are needed. For 21 of the sub-targets data were lacking to make an assessment.
The Riksdag welcomes the communication and notes that considerable progress has been made with regard to the goals, both within Sweden and globally. The Riksdag further notes that Sweden has a good starting position and better conditions for achieving the global goals than many other countries. The Riksdag considers, however, that there is a considerable way still to go for Sweden before the goals are met.
The Riksdag filed the communication — that is, closed the matter.

The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2021/22:4768 by Ali Esbati et al. (V) items 1–8 and 

2021/22:4769 by Elisabeth Svantesson et al. (M) items 1–4 and 

files government communication 2021/22:247.

dok_titel: Report on the distribution of funds from the General Inheritance Fund during the fiscal year 2021
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2022/23:29 by Ulrika Westerlund (MP) items 1–3.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered the Government's communication on the administration of the General Inheritance Fund (Allmänna arvsfonden) and how the Inheritance Fund Delegation (Arvsfondsdelegationen) has distributed funds from the fund during 2021.
The Riksdag agrees with the Government that funds from the General Inheritance Fund have been distributed in a good manner and in line with the fund's purposes and priority areas.
The Government also considers that, even during the COVID-19 pandemic, the Inheritance Fund Delegation largely succeeded in fulfilling its mandate, although applications decreased during 2021. With the decrease as one of the factors, the Government considers it important to continue the work of increasing awareness and knowledge of the inheritance fund. The Riksdag shares the Government's assessment that there is a continued need to increase the number of applications across the country and that the positive results generated by the projects are disseminated nationally.
The capital of the General Inheritance Fund comes primarily from estates of persons who die without leaving a spouse or closer relatives than cousins and have not bequeathed the property to anyone else.
The Inheritance Fund Delegation is the authority that, among other things, makes decisions on and monitors the projects that receive funds from the General Inheritance Fund.
The Riksdag rejected a motion in the area and thereby noted the communication, i.e., concluded the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2022/23:29 by Ulrika Westerlund (MP) items 1–3.
Reservation 1

rubrik: Amendments to the new Riksbank Act
dok_titel: A new Riksbank Act (dormant constitutional proposals etc.)
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) items 1–3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the dormant proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen) and the Riksdag Act (riksdagsordningen) concerning the Riksbank, and the Government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act. The proposals for amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Riksdag Act are so-called dormant proposals (vilande förslag), meaning that the Riksdag has previously voted on the matter. The amendments to the Instrument of Government include, among other things, a clarification of the Riksbank's duties. The proposed amendment to the Riksdag Act makes clear that the Riksdag's Committee on Finance shall follow up and evaluate the Riksbank's operations.
The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposal for a new Riksbank Act, but with some minor amendments. The new Riksbank Act entails, among other things:

The Riksbank's objectives, tasks and powers are clarified with regard to monetary policy, the financial system, means of payment, peacetime crisis situations and heightened alert, and international activities
It shall become clearer how the Riksbank's areas of responsibility relate to each other and to those of Finansinspektionen (the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority) and Riksgäldskontoret (the Swedish National Debt Office)
It shall become clearer that the Riksbank, within the framework of monetary policy, shall take real-economic considerations into account, and conditions are created for a democratic anchoring of the specification of the price stability target
The basic structure of the Riksbank's organisation is retained, but the number of members of the Executive Board (direktionen) is reduced from six to five. A more appropriate division of responsibilities is introduced between the General Council (riksbanksfullmäktige), the Executive Board and the Governor (riksbankschefen)
The Riksbank's position as an independent central bank and independent administrative authority is strengthened
The Riksbank's financial independence is strengthened in the framework of, for example, disposing of profits and structuring its own capital, and borrowing for the foreign exchange reserve
The conditions for transparency and scrutiny of the Riksbank's operations are improved
The Riksbank shall contribute to sustainable development in the financial market.

Since the proposals in certain parts concern amendments to the Instrument of Government and the Riksdag Act, the Riksdag is required to vote identically on two occasions with a general election in between. The first decision on the proposals was taken on 1 June 2022, when the Riksdag voted yes. A general election has since taken place.
All legislative amendments are to enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2021/22:4297 by Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) items 1–3.

rubrik: The future regulation of the dispute resolution procedure
dok_titel: An independent dispute resolution procedure for collective rental disputes
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2022/23:13 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) items 1 and 2.
notis:
The previous Government submitted a proposal on dispute resolution in certain collective rental negotiations. This entails, among other things, a new independent dispute resolution body for the entire rental market and tightened rules for rental negotiations.
The parties in the rental market regularly conduct collective negotiations on the general level of rents. Such negotiations are often referred to as the annual rent negotiations. When these negotiations are prolonged, it can entail financial risks for the parties involved.
Within the public housing stock, there is currently a dispute resolution body, the Rental Market Committee (Hyresmarknadskommittén, HMK). A corresponding solution is now to be introduced for the entire rental market, including the private rental stock. If the parties cannot agree on the annual rent adjustment, a special arbitrator may be appointed to examine the dispute. The aim is to make collective negotiations more efficient and for the annual rent negotiations to be concluded more quickly.
Tightened rules for negotiation meetings are also introduced. Among other things, a party may be held liable for damages if it does not attend a negotiation meeting that is to be held within a certain period.
The Riksdag approved the proposal. The new rules enter into force on 1 January 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects Motion

2022/23:13 by Malcolm Momodou Jallow et al. (V) items 1 and 2.
Reservation 1

In its report, Riksrevisionen makes a number of recommendations to the government and to Lantmäteriet (the Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority).
In the communication, the government welcomes the review and considers Riksrevisionen's report to be an important contribution to the ongoing work aimed at developing and improving property formation. Digitalisation is assessed to be the measure that will have the greatest impact on processing times in property formation, and work toward that development should be prioritised. There may also be reason to review parts of Lantmäteriet's fee model. With the communication, the government considers Riksrevisionen's report to be fully addressed.
The Riksdag filed the government's communication, that is, closed the matter.

rubrik: Assignment of coordination numbers to asylum seekers
dok_titel: A strengthened system for coordination numbers
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) item 2.
notis:
The Riksdag endorses the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) and also for amendments to, among other things, the Population Registration Act and the Population Registration Database Act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, raising the requirements for the identity checks carried out before a coordination number is issued to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not, or have not been, registered in Sweden's population register (folkbokförda), but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons who are registered in Sweden's population register are instead assigned a personal identity number (personnummer).
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check was carried out beforehand. Currently there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number may be issued at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also appear in person at the time of application. The identity documents may also be requested for verification of the biometric data stored in them.
The proposal also means that Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency) takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities must notify Skatteverket if it can be assumed that a piece of information in the population registration database is incorrect in relation to persons with coordination numbers.
The proposal also includes a restriction on the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The legislative amendments concerning those locally employed at embassies and consulates are to enter into force on 1 January 2023, and the remaining ones on 1 September 2023.

dok_titel: Copyright on the digital single market
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:27 by Elin Söderberg and Amanda Lind (both MP) item 3.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposals for amendments to, among other things, the Copyright Act (upphovsrättslagen). The proposals are based on an EU directive and contain new rules aimed at adapting copyright law to digital developments.
As digital technology enables new forms of use of copyright-protected material, Swedish copyright legislation needs to be modernised. The government's proposals entail, among other things, exceptions to copyright law to facilitate teaching and research, but also to enable the preservation of cultural heritage. They also introduce new provisions allowing the free reproduction of older works of art.
The proposal also means that press publishers will be able to receive remuneration when their material is reused on the internet. There will also be new provisions regulating liability when users themselves upload material to various digital platforms. The providers of these services and platforms are to conclude agreements with rights holders who wish to do so, but must also be obliged to act when material is uploaded against the rights holder's wishes.
Finally, a number of rules are introduced to strengthen the contractual position of creators when they transfer their rights to publishers, producers, newspapers or other actors in the copyright market.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023.

notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication from the government concerning the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) review of processing times in asylum cases at Sweden's migration courts.
Riksrevisionen's overall conclusion is that case management has efficiency shortcomings and that the migration courts are far from reaching the target of deciding 90 per cent of asylum cases within four months. Riksrevisionen also made recommendations to the Courts Administration (Domstolsverket) and the government on measures to reduce processing times.
In its communication, the government concurs with Riksrevisionen's observations and at the same time points to measures that have been taken and that the government will follow up on.
The Riksdag assumes that the government will follow up on the measures and that the Courts Administration will continue its efficiency-improvement work. With that, the Riksdag filed the government's communication, that is, closed the matter.

rubrik: Exemption from the duty to notify
dok_titel: A strengthened system for coordination numbers
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion 

2022/23:16 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) item 4.
notis:
The Riksdag endorses the proposal for a new law on coordination numbers (samordningsnummer) and also for amendments to, among other things, the Population Registration Act and the Population Registration Database Act. The purpose is to strengthen the system for coordination numbers by, for example, raising the requirements for the identity checks carried out before a coordination number is issued to a person.
A coordination number is an identity designation for persons who are not, or have not been, registered in Sweden's population register (folkbokförda), but who still need to have contact with Swedish authorities or other parts of society. Persons who are registered in Sweden's population register are instead assigned a personal identity number (personnummer).
Coordination numbers are divided into different levels depending on which identity check was carried out beforehand. Currently there are two levels. Under the new law, a coordination number may be issued at three different levels. To obtain the highest level, the person must be able to prove their identity with valid identity documents and also appear in person at the time of application. The identity documents may also be requested for verification of the biometric data stored in them.
The proposal also means that Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency) takes over responsibility for, among other things, identity checks when a coordination number is to be assigned to a person. Other authorities must notify Skatteverket if it can be assumed that a piece of information in the population registration database is incorrect in relation to persons with coordination numbers.
The proposal also includes a restriction on the exemption from population registration that applies to persons who are locally employed at foreign embassies or consulates in Sweden.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal.
The legislative amendments concerning those locally employed at embassies and consulates are to enter into force on 1 January 2023, and the remaining ones on 1 September 2023.

rubrik: The guidelines for economic policy and fiscal policy
dok_titel: The State Budget 2023 – The Framework Decision
forslag_text:
The Riksdag approves the guidelines for economic policy and fiscal policy proposed by the Government. 
The Riksdag thereby approves proposition 2022/23:1 the fiscal plan point 1 and rejects motions 

2022/23:1299 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) item 1, 

2022/23:2074 by Magdalena Andersson et al. (S) item 1, 

2022/23:2180 by Annie Lööf et al. (C) item 1 and 

2022/23:2275 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) item 1.
notis:
The Government has put forward proposals for expenditure frameworks and revenue estimates for the state budget in the Budget Bill for 2023. Expenditure is estimated at SEK 1 195 billion and revenue is estimated at SEK 1 279 billion. This represents a surplus in the state budget of SEK 84 billion for 2023. The expenditure ceiling for the state is SEK 1 665 billion for 2023, SEK 1 745 billion for 2024 and SEK 1 825 billion for 2025.
The Budget Bill also contains proposals on tax and fee rules relating to, among other things:

an enhanced earned income tax credit (jobbskatteavdrag) for persons over the age of 65
increased tax on alcohol and tobacco
an enhanced tax reduction for the installation of solar panels
a temporary reduction in tax on motor fuels
a reduction in tax on fuels used in certain heat production
a maintained travel expense deduction with certain enhancements for commuting, business travel and home travel.

Some of these proposals have been presented in their own bills, but are announced in the Budget Bill and are included in the revenue estimates for the budget.
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposals on the spending frameworks for the state budget for 2023. The Riksdag's decision on the spending frameworks for the state budget then governs the Riksdag's next step of deciding on the appropriations for the 27 expenditure areas in the budget.
All legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023, except for the decisions concerning the abolition of the tax reduction for data centres and a clearer chemicals tax, which enter into force on 1 July 2023. With regard to the increased tax on alcohol and tobacco, the legislative amendments enter into force on 1 January 2023 and 1 January 2024 respectively.
The Riksdag also approved the Government's direction for economic policy and fiscal policy.
GDP grew relatively strongly during the first half of 2022, but growth is expected to slow going forward. Growth is assessed to turn negative next year and the Swedish economy is expected to be in a recession during 2023. Fiscal policy should be mildly restrictive so as not to counteract monetary policy at a time when high inflation could become entrenched.
In the near term, policy should focus on measures that support businesses and households under pressure from rising prices. This includes, among other things, a temporary high-cost protection for electricity costs and an extension of the temporary extra contribution to families with children receiving housing benefit. Temporary tax reductions on motor fuels are to ease the consequences for those who are dependent on their car in rural areas and for businesses in agriculture and forestry. General government grants to municipalities and regions are being strengthened.
The Riksdag made its decision in the matter despite the fact that the matter had been available for less than two working days before the day on which it was considered, which is the usual requirement.

rubrik: Subsidiarity review of the Commission's proposal for a regulation establishing a crisis instrument for the internal market
dok_titel: Subsidiarity review of the Commission's proposal for a regulation establishing a crisis instrument for the internal market
forslag_text: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission, with the wording set out in the committee's proposal in Annex 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has reviewed a legislative proposal from the EU Commission concerning the introduction of an instrument aimed at ensuring that the internal market within the EU — that is, the free movement of persons, goods, and services — functions well even in crisis situations. The proposal also includes provisions on securing the availability of goods and services of strategic importance, which under the proposal is defined as goods and services that are absolutely necessary for the internal market and that cannot be substituted or diversified. The proposal has been reviewed under the so-called subsidiarity principle, which states that the EU should only legislate on an issue if the objectives of the proposed measure cannot be achieved equally well or better by the member states themselves.
The Riksdag considers that the proposal is not in all respects compatible with the subsidiarity principle. According to the Riksdag, there is a need to clarify how the provisions on goods and services of strategic importance relate to the legal basis specified. The Riksdag therefore decided to raise objections to the European Parliament, the Council of Ministers, and the EU Commission in a so-called reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande).
alternatives: The Riksdag decides to submit a reasoned opinion (motiverat yttrande) to the Presidents of the European Parliament, the Council, and the Commission, with the wording set out in the committee's proposal in Annex 2.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2022/23:2297 by Helena Lindahl et al. (C).
notis:
To address the rapidly rising energy prices, the EU has decided on a so-called solidarity contribution. The idea is that companies within the Union that deal with fossil fuels and make large profits should pay a solidarity contribution.
The money is to be used by member states to pay out financial support to private individuals and companies that have been severely affected by high energy prices. In Sweden, the government proposes a temporary tax on extraordinary profits for certain companies in the fossil sector. The temporary tax is to correspond to the EU's solidarity contribution and is to be levied in 2023.
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal for a temporary tax to mitigate the consequences of high energy prices. The temporary law comes into force on 1 January 2023.

forslag_text:

The Riksdag thereby approves the motions

notis:
The Riksdag rejected the government's proposal on amended conditions when regions enter into contracts with private healthcare providers that also have insurance companies as clients. The government's proposal concerns amendments to the Health and Medical Care Act (hälso- och sjukvårdslagen) and means that the contract must set out how it is ensured that the private healthcare provider's other assignments do not have a negative impact on the care provided on behalf of the region.
The Riksdag approved the proposal in the Health and Medical Care Act that rehabilitation is to be included in primary care's core assignment.

Such an injunction may be combined with a fine (vite).
The amendments to the Patient Safety Act enter into force on 1 July 2023. The amendment to the Health and Medical Care Act enters into force on 1 January 2024.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the government's proposed amendment to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act (offentlighets- och sekretesslagen) (2009:400) in the parts concerning Chapter 28, Section 4 b.
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2022/23:48 point 1 in this part and rejects the motions 

2022/23:2304 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) in this part, 

2022/23:2305 by Malin Björk et al. (C) in this part and 

2022/23:2306 by Per Bolund et al. (MP) in this part.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the government's proposal that secrecy is to apply when the Swedish Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan) processes matters concerning electricity support for electricity users. Secrecy is to apply to electricity users' personal circumstances and to data used to identify electrical installations. If it is clear that the information can be disclosed without causing harm to any individual, secrecy shall not apply.
The Riksdag also approved the proposal to remove the Swedish Social Insurance Agency's obligation to submit a control statement (kontrolluppgift) to the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) in matters concerning electricity support for electricity users.
The legislative amendments enter into force on 1 February 2023.

rubrik: The Swedish National Audit Office's report on the annual adjustment of government agency appropriations
dok_titel: The Swedish National Audit Office's report on the annual adjustment of government agency appropriations
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:10 by Janine Alm Ericson (MP) and 

2022/23:1299 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V) item 9 and 

notes communication 2021/22:241.
notis:
The Riksdag notes that the legitimacy of the annual adjustment of government agency appropriations rests on it being transparent and predictable, and therefore views positively the government's continuous work to increase transparency both in the model itself and in the information about the price and wage adjustment.
Each year, government agencies are allocated appropriations from the state budget to finance, among other things, salaries and premises. Before each new budget year, the Ministry of Finance recalculates the appropriations so that agencies are not affected by price and wage increases in the wider economy.
The price and wage adjustment model (also known as PLO) was introduced approximately 30 years ago and the calculation is carried out automatically so that the state's role as an employer is kept separate from the government's political priorities. In order for agencies to achieve productivity growth in line with the private service sector, a so-called productivity deduction is applied.
It is in response to the Swedish National Audit Office's examination of the PLO and the productivity deduction that the government has submitted a communication (skrivelse). The examination shows, among other things, that the built-in productivity requirement has functioned as a steering signal for efficiency improvements and that it has not prevented agencies from carrying out their mandates.
The Riksdag noted the government's communication, i.e. closed the matter.

The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:10 by Janine Alm Ericson (MP) and

notes communication 2021/22:241.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motions

2022/23:2287 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) and

2022/23:2292 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) items 1 and 2.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication (skrivelse) from the government. It concerns the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionens) review of the Medical Products Agency's (Läkemedelsverkets) supervision of community pharmacies and wholesale trade in medicines. The report covers supervision by the Medical Products Agency (Läkemedelsverket), the Health and Social Care Inspectorate (Inspektionen för vård och omsorg, Ivo) and the Dental and Pharmaceutical Benefits Agency (Tandvårds- och läkemedelsförmånsverket, TLV).
The Swedish National Audit Office's conclusion is that the state's supervision of the pharmacy sector and trade in medicines is not effective. This may lead to both pharmacies and those who buy and sell medicines risking operating in a manner that does not meet legal requirements. The consequence may then be that patient safety suffers and that the costs to the state and the regions become unnecessarily large.
In the communication, the government welcomes the review and is positively disposed towards several of the measures proposed by the Swedish National Audit Office. Among other things, the government considers that there are grounds for examining whether provisions should be introduced to prevent pharmacies from charging excessive prices for medicines not included in the pharmaceutical benefits scheme (läkemedelsförmånerna) but subsidised by the state or the regions, and for special dietary products for children.
The Riksdag broadly shares the government's assessments and considers it essential that supervision can be carried out effectively. With this, the Riksdag noted the communication, i.e. closed the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motions

2022/23:2287 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V) and

rubrik: Increased value added tax on certain repairs
dok_titel: Increased value added tax on certain repairs
forslag_text:
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for an act amending the Value Added Tax Act (1994:200).
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2022/23:35 and rejects the motions 

2022/23:2308 by Ilona Szatmári Waldau et al. (V) and 

2022/23:2312 by Marielle Lahti et al. (MP).
notis:
The Riksdag voted in favour of the Government's proposal to raise VAT on repairs of bicycles, shoes, leather goods, clothing and household linen from 6 percent to 12 percent. The purpose is to increase uniformity in the tax system.
Through the proposed tax increase, the difference in tax take between these repair services and other repair services covered by the standard rate of 25 percent will be reduced. The Government considers that VAT is an efficient tax that should be protected as a source of revenue for the state and that the starting point should therefore be uniform VAT and application of the standard rate.
The new rules enter into force on 1 April 2023.

forslag_text:
Amendments to the state budget for 2023
The Riksdag approves the revised calculation of revenues in the state budget for 2023 in accordance with the Government's proposal.
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2022/23:58 item 3.

Legislation underlying the amendment to the state budget 
The Riksdag adopts the Government's proposal for

2. an act amending the Tax Procedures Act (2011:1244).
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2022/23:58 items 1 and 2.

Future additions to the Government's legislative proposal

2022/23:2335 by Martin Ådahl and Rickard Nordin (both C) and 

2022/23:2336 by Marielle Lahti and Annika Hirvonen (both MP).
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for a new act enabling a temporary tax on excess revenues from certain electricity production. The proposal means that revenues exceeding 1,957 kronor per megawatt-hour will be taxed at 90 percent during the period March–June 2023. The proposal was submitted in the form of a supplementary amending budget for 2023.
The proposal is based on an EU regulation containing several measures to address the high energy prices in Europe. One of the measures is a so-called temporary cap on excess revenues from electricity production. Member states may determine the exact level of the cap within a certain range.
The temporary tax covers electricity producers with an installed capacity of more than 1 megawatt. Wind power and nuclear power will primarily be affected. The tax is estimated to increase state revenues by 362 million kronor in 2023. The act enters into force on 1 March 2023.

It concerns the Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) review of the Medical Products Agency's (Läkemedelsverket) supervision of open-care pharmacies and the wholesale trade in medicines. The report covers supervision by the Medical Products Agency (Läkemedelsverket), the Health and Social Care Inspectorate (Inspektionen för vård och omsorg, Ivo), and the Dental and Pharmaceutical Benefits Agency (Tandvårds- och läkemedelsförmånsverket, TLV).
The Swedish National Audit Office's conclusion is that the state's supervision of the pharmacy sector and trade in medicines is not effective. This may lead to a situation where both pharmacies and those who buy and sell medicines risk operating in ways that do not meet the requirements of the law. The consequence could then be that patient safety suffers and that expenditure for the state and the regions becomes unnecessarily large.
In the written communication, the Government welcomes the review and takes a positive view of several of the measures proposed by the Swedish National Audit Office. Among other things, the Government considers that there are grounds to consider whether provisions should be introduced to prevent pharmacies from charging excessive prices for medicines not covered by the pharmaceutical benefits scheme (läkemedelsförmånerna) but subsidised by the state or the regions, and for special dietary foods for children.
The Riksdag largely shares the Government's assessments and considers it essential that supervision can be carried out effectively. With this, the Riksdag noted the written communication, i.e. concluded the matter.

rubrik: The future regulation of land acquisition legislation
dok_titel: Amendments to the Agricultural Land Acquisition Act aimed at preventing circumvention of the provisions on acquisition permits
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:985 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) item 43.
notis:
The Riksdag approved the Government's proposal for amendments to the Agricultural Land Acquisition Act (jordförvärvslagen). The legislative amendments mean that the definition of agricultural property is expanded to cover not only real property classified as an agricultural unit for property assessment purposes but also real property that has been converted or newly formed for the purpose of agriculture or forestry but has not yet been subject to property assessment.
One purpose of the Agricultural Land Acquisition Act is to maintain the balance in land holdings between private individuals and legal entities with regard to agricultural properties. For this reason, a so-called acquisition permit (förvärvstillstånd) is required when legal entities such as a company wish to acquire an agricultural property.
The narrow definition of what constitutes agricultural property has, in several high-profile cases, allowed legal entities to acquire property from natural persons without the provisions on acquisition permits becoming applicable. That is why the Government considers that the rules should be changed.
The new rules are proposed to take effect on 15 April 2023.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:985 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD) item 43.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:2301 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) items 1–4 and

2022/23:2302 by Ulrika Westerlund (MP) items 1–4.
notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication (skrivelse) from the Government. The communication contains a report on the Government's work on healthcare issues. It is a response to a tillkännagivande (formal request to the Government) made by the Riksdag on 23 March 2022. The tillkännagivande called on the then Government to take measures to, among other things, increase the number of hospital beds and shorten waiting times in healthcare.
The previous Government had previously reported back to the Riksdag with two communications. The Riksdag assessed at that time that the Government had implemented some of the measures listed in the tillkännagivande. The new communication is submitted by the current Government, which took office after the election in September 2022.
The Government has thus completed its reporting to the Riksdag. The Riksdag considers, with reference to, among other things, the 2023 budget and the Tidöavtalet (the Tidö agreement), that the Government has demonstrated that it is aware of the need to improve healthcare. The tillkännagivande on healthcare issues has therefore been fully addressed.
The Riksdag noted the communication, that is, closed the matter.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:2300 by Karin Rågsjö et al. (V),

2022/23:2301 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) items 1–4 and

notis:
The Riksdag has considered a communication from the Government on national infrastructure planning for 2022–2033. In response to a claim in a consequential motion to the communication, the Riksdag issued a tillkännagivande (formal request) to the Government to reject the construction of high-speed rail.
In response to claims in two motions from the general motions period of 2022, the Riksdag issued a further tillkännagivande to the Government, stating that the interim target for greenhouse gas emissions from domestic transport should be maintained. It is important that the management of contaminated areas and the work to reduce the negative impact of infrastructure on the natural environment and cultural landscape continue, and that the pace of the transport sector's transition to fossil-free energy increases.
The Riksdag rejected the remaining motions from the general motions period of 2022 on various infrastructure issues, such as roads and railways. The Riksdag considered, among other things, that work is already under way in the areas addressed by the motions.

The Riksdag issued a request, a so-called tillkännagivande (formal request to the government), to the government for expanded investments in wetlands. The request builds on proposals in motion items from the general motion period 2022 on water management. According to the Riksdag, this work needs to continue and be strengthened, as wetlands play a major role in climate work and contribute to, among other things, strengthening biodiversity and combating eutrophication in seas and lakes.

The Riksdag considers, among other things, that work is already ongoing in the areas addressed by the motions.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag 
a) approves 
1. Sweden's accession to the North Atlantic Treaty,
2. the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, national representatives, and the organisation's international staff,
b) adopts the Government's proposal for an act amending the Act (1976:661) on Immunity and Privileges in Certain Cases.
The Riksdag thereby approves Government Bill 2022/23:74, points 1-3, and rejects the motions 

2022/23:2348 by Håkan Svenneling et al. (V), item 1 in this part and item 2, and 

2022/23:2349 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP), item 1 in this part and item 2.
notis:
The Riksdag approved Sweden's accession to the North Atlantic Treaty and the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO). The status agreement regulates immunity and privileges for NATO and certain categories of personnel. The Riksdag also approved the Government's proposal for legislative amendments.
Sweden's application to join NATO requires amendments to two acts: the Act on Operational Military Support and the Act on Immunity and Privileges in Certain Cases. The legislative amendments are intended partly to make it easier for Sweden to request support from NATO in the form of military forces, and partly to give NATO, the national representatives, and the international staff the immunity and privileges required under the agreement.
Regarding the decision on the Act on Operational Military Support, the decision must be made with a majority of at least three-quarters, and more than half of the members of the Riksdag must vote in favour of the proposal. This is required under the Instrument of Government (regeringsformen), since the decision involves transferring the exercise of public authority to another state.
The legislative amendments will enter into force on the date determined by the Government.
alternatives:

a) approves

2. the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, national representatives, and the organisation's international staff,

forslag_text:

2022/23:2349 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP), items 3-9.
notis:
The Riksdag approved Sweden's accession to the North Atlantic Treaty and the agreement on the status of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, NATO. The status agreement regulates immunity and privileges for NATO and certain categories of personnel. The Riksdag also said yes to the Government's proposed legislative amendments.
With the application to NATO, amendments are required to two laws: the Act on Operational Military Support and the Act on Immunity and Privileges in Certain Cases. The legislative amendments aim partly to make it easier for Sweden to request support from NATO in the form of military forces, and partly to give NATO, the national representatives, and the international staff the immunity and privileges required under the agreement.
Regarding the decision on the Act on Operational Military Support, the decision must be made by at least a three-quarters majority, and more than half of the members of the Riksdag must vote in favor of the proposal. This follows from the Instrument of Government, since the decision concerns transferring the exercise of public authority to another state.
The legislative amendments are to enter into force on the date determined by the Government.

rubrik: A new system for resource allocation
dok_titel: The Swedish National Audit Office's report The School Voucher – Efficiency and Consequences
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:610 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V), item 5, 

2022/23:884 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C), item 32, 

2022/23:2128 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S), item 4, 

2022/23:2313 by Åsa Westlund et al. (S), items 1-4 and 

2022/23:2318 by Muharrem Demirok et al. (C), items 1-4.
notis:
The Swedish National Audit Office's (Riksrevisionen) review of the school voucher (skolpengen) paid to independent schools shows that the rules on compensation to individual education providers (enskilda huvudmän) in certain respects work against an equal school system and therefore need to be changed. In a communication, the Government states that it largely shares the conclusions of the review and that the issues are to be investigated further. The Riksdag places the Government's communication on file, that is, closes the matter.
The school voucher is the sum of money that a pupil generates for the education provider responsible for that pupil's schooling. The Swedish National Audit Office considers that the current rules make it difficult for education providers to plan their operations and to achieve an efficient allocation of resources. It therefore recommends that the Government ensure that a state-determined standard model is introduced for compensation to individual education providers.
In addition, the Swedish National Audit Office recommends that the Government review the regulations on significant negative consequences arising from the establishment of independent schools, so that it becomes clear what is meant.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:610 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V), item 5,

dok_titel: Better opportunities for the Swedish Tax Agency to carry out data analyses and selections in population registration activities
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:123 by Anna Vikström (S), 

2022/23:292 by Jan Ericson (M), 

2022/23:961 by Magnus Persson et al. (SD), item 10, and 

2022/23:1022 by Per Söderlund et al. (SD), item 27.
notis:
The Swedish Tax Agency is to be given better opportunities to reduce the amount of errors and fraud in the population register. This is in order to counteract crime directed against, among other things, the welfare systems. The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal.
Through the legislative amendments, the Swedish Tax Agency is allowed to process personal data in order to carry out data analyses and selections with the aim of preventing, hindering and detecting incorrect information in the population register. The agency is to target areas with a high risk of errors and fraud and where the best possible effect can be achieved.
For the data collected for analysis and selection, new regulations are introduced, which aim, among other things, to reduce the intrusion into personal privacy that the proposals may entail. For example, special rules are introduced on the maximum period for processing personal data, as well as strong confidentiality protection.
The legislative amendments concerning data analyses and selections, and the amendment to the Act on Risk Tax for Credit Institutions, take effect on 1 May 2023. The other legislative amendments take effect on 1 September 2023.

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motion 

2022/23:1882 by Malin Björk et al. (C), item 4.
notis:
The Riksdag said no to 18 proposals concerning the Riksdag's working procedures. The proposals were submitted during the 2022 general motion period. The motions deal with, among other things, the opening of the parliamentary session, the right to submit motions, and the financial conditions of Riksdag members.
The Riksdag directs a so-called tillkännagivande (formal request) to the Riksdag Board (Riksdagsstyrelsen). The request concerns having the Riksdag Board set up an inquiry to review the question of the Government's consultation with the EU Affairs Committee on the EU's A-points. At the meetings of the Council of the European Union, there are A-points and B-points on the agenda. A-points are characterised by the fact that agreement is possible without debate, while B-points require discussion among the member states. The Riksdag's Parliamentary EU Committee has previously pointed out that the consultation in the Riksdag concerning the A-points could be improved.
alternatives:

2022/23:1882 by Malin Björk et al. (C), item 4.

2022/23:181 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP), item 30.
notis:
The Riksdag rejected 14 proposals in motions from the 2022 general motion period concerning public access to information, confidentiality and privacy. This was mainly with reference to ongoing work and to rules already in force in the area.
The motions concern, among other things, information exchange between public authorities, confidentiality in cases regarding the appointment of municipal and regional directors, disclosure of the so-called Stasi archives, trade in personal data, an inquiry into greater control over how the public sector uses personal data, application of the principle of public access to official documents (offentlighetsprincipen), and artificial intelligence and privacy.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motion

2022/23:181 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP), item 30.
Reservation 5 (a formal dissenting opinion filed by a minority on the committee)

forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions

2022/23:303 by John E Weinerhall and Viktor Wärnick (both M), and

2022/23:936 by Tobias Andersson et al. (SD), items 17 and 18.
notis:
The Riksdag issued a formal request (tillkännagivande) to the Government concerning the role of public authorities in permit processes. The committee considers that authorities involved in permit processes should work in a more advisory and solution-oriented manner than before. The request is based on a proposal in a motion from the 2022 general motion period on mineral policy issues.
The Riksdag rejected around 40 proposals in the remaining motions. These concern, among other things, permits and permit processes, bans on extraction, property rights and compensation, as well as so-called innovation-critical metals and minerals.
alternatives:

rubrik: Follow-up on the effects of the legislative proposal
dok_titel: Certain issues concerning the supply preparedness of health and medical care
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:2327 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) and 

2022/23:2329 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S), item 3.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the government's legislative proposal to clarify requirements on care providers that operate health and medical care activities. This means they must provide health care products needed to be able to give good care. Health care products refers to medicines, medical devices, personal protective equipment, food for special medical purposes, and manufacturing materials.
The proposals also mean that community pharmacies have an obligation to stock medicines, and wholesalers have a delivery obligation towards hospital pharmacies. A sanction fee is introduced for companies that fail to notify the Medical Products Agency that sales of a medicine are being discontinued temporarily or permanently. Information on any shortage in the supply of a medicine or medical device is proposed to be eligible for protection under confidentiality when the information is transferred from the Medical Products Agency to regions or municipalities in connection with an investigation.
The legislative amendments are to take effect on 1 July 2023.
The Riksdag also said yes to the government's proposal that the state-owned company Apotek Produktion & Laboratorier AB be given an expanded public service mission. This means the company must maintain its operations even during peacetime crises, heightened alert, and ultimately war. This could, for example, mean ensuring the supply of active substances, excipients, and packaging materials for products needed for care that cannot wait.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:2327 by Anders W Jonsson et al. (C) and 

2022/23:2329 by Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S), item 3.
Reservation 3 (dissenting opinion)

notis:
The Riksdag issued an appeal, a so-called formal request (tillkännagivande), to the Government to take measures for a more well-functioning, efficient and legally secure system for division of property (bodelning) upon divorce. For the party who is worst off financially, it is usually of very great economic importance that the division of property is completed. However, the other party often benefits from the division of property being drawn out over time, which has been established in an inquiry.
The Riksdag notes that the Government is to begin mapping how large the problem of protracted division-of-property processes is. The Riksdag welcomes this and considers it high time for the Government to move forward on the issue. Among other things, the Government should review the possibility of introducing a reasonable final deadline for when a division of property should be completed.
The formal request is based on several proposals in motions submitted during the general motion period of 2022. In total, the Riksdag has considered around 130 proposals on various family law issues, which also concern, among other things, the legal regulation of parenthood, the reflection period before divorce, and various custody issues. The Riksdag rejected the other motions, citing among other things that the Government is already working on these issues.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects motions 

2022/23:245 by Nadja Awad et al. (V) point 8, 

2022/23:949 by Mikael Eskilandersson et al. (SD) points 21 and 22, and

2022/23:2218 by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S) items 2 and 3 and 

2022/23:2277 by Märta Stenevi et al. (MP) items 115 and 116.
notis:
The Riksdag addressed a formal request, a so-called tillkännagivande (formal request), to the government to take measures for a more well-functioning, efficient and legally secure system for the division of property between spouses. For the party who is worse off financially, it is usually of great economic importance that the division of property is completed. However, one party often benefits from the division of property being drawn out over time, which has been established in an inquiry.
The Riksdag notes that the government is to begin mapping out how large the problem of protracted division-of-property processes is. The Riksdag welcomes this and believes it is high time the government moves forward on the issue. Among other things, the government should review the possibility of introducing a reasonable final time limit for when a division of property should be completed.
The formal request is based on several proposals in motions submitted during the 2022 general motion period. In total, the Riksdag has dealt with about 130 proposals on various family-law issues, which also concern, among other things, the legal regulation of parenthood, the reflection period before divorce, and various custody issues. The Riksdag rejected the other motions, citing among other things that the government is already working on the issues.

dok_titel: Implementation of the Electricity Market Directive regarding the supply of electricity and aggregation services
forslag_text:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:998 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD), item 7, and 

2022/23:1235 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V), items 1-3.
notis:
The Riksdag said yes to the Government's proposal on how the EU's Electricity Market Directive, as regards the supply of electricity and so-called aggregation services, is to be implemented in Swedish legislation.
The directive aims to adapt the electricity market to new conditions brought about by a more decentralised production of electricity from renewable sources and the phasing-out of fossil fuels.
The Government's proposal means greater opportunity for electricity users to adjust their electricity consumption when the price of electricity is low or when the electricity grid is heavily loaded. The proposal also involves changes to certain requirements on electricity suppliers, as well as changes to the rules on switching electricity supplier for small businesses. Under the proposal, the Government, or the authority designated by the Government, will also be able to determine rules on the information that electricity suppliers must provide to electricity users.
In 2022, the Riksdag decided to implement the parts of the Electricity Market Directive concerning grid operations in Swedish legislation. The Electricity Market Directive was to have been implemented in its entirety in Swedish legislation by 31 December 2020 at the latest. The European Commission has initiated infringement proceedings against Sweden for the late implementation of the Electricity Market Directive.
The Riksdag also approved an addition to the Government's proposal concerning a so-called normgivningsbemyndigande (an authorization empowering the Government to issue binding regulations). Such an authorization is needed so that the Government can determine rules on various administrative processes — for example, that grid companies must send notifications to electricity suppliers when the supply of electricity begins or is taken over.
Finally, the Riksdag said no to 80 proposals in motions from the general motion period of 2022.
alternatives:
The Riksdag rejects the motions 

2022/23:998 by Martin Kinnunen et al. (SD), item 7, and 

2022/23:1235 by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (V), items 1-3.
Reservation 6
